extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent prosecutors, and patent applicants (practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners and applicants on handling final Office actions, withdrawal of finality, transitional after-final submissions (37 CFR 1.129), timing for replies and extensions, examiner’s amendments, and Request for Continued Examination (RCE) practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action is final after filing CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the parent application prior to the filing of this Continued Prosecution Application under 37 CFR 1.53(d) and could have been finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action after the filing under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is reminded of the extension of time policy as set forth in 37 CFR 1.136(a). Use appropriate form paragraph (e.g., 7.41.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prematurity of final rejection is practice question, not appealable
rubrics_metrics.description: Any question as to prematureness of a final rejection should be raised, if at all, while the application is still pending before the primary examiner. This is purely a question of practice, wholly distinct from the tenability of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prematureness may not be advanced as a ground for appeal or complaint before the Board; it is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181. See MPEP § 1002.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality when rejection is premature
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on request by applicant for reconsideration, the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature, he or she should withdraw the finality of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The finality must be withdrawn while the application is still pending; cannot be withdrawn once application is abandoned. Once finality is withdrawn, the next Office action may be made final if conditions of MPEP § 706.07(a) are met. Use form paragraph 7.42 when withdrawing finality of last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of final rejection — general limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, it should not be withdrawn at the applicant’s or owner’s request except on a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further amendment or argument may be considered in certain instances. An amendment that places the application in condition for allowance or better form for appeal may be admitted. Examiner may withdraw rejection if new facts/reasons convince allowance or patentability (including in reexamination). Withdrawal to apply a new ground of rejection is permissible only in limited circumstances (new reference fully meets at least one claim or differences shown to be completely obvious). Practice should not be used for subsidiary, cumulative, or merely 'better' references. When a final rejection is withdrawn, amendments filed after final are ordinarily entered. New grounds reopening prosecution after appeal brief require supervisory patent examiner approval (see MPEP § 1002.02(d)). See MPEP § 714.12 and § 714.13 for amendments after final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable reply period and shortened statutory period (SSP) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All final rejections setting a 3-month shortened statutory period (SSP) for reply should contain specified form paragraphs advising applicant that if the reply is filed within 2 months of the date of the final Office action, the shortened statutory period will expire at 3 months from the date of the final rejection or on the date the advisory action is mailed, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 2-month last day falls on a weekend/holiday, a reply filed on the next business day is deemed within 2 months under 37 CFR 1.7(a). In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the mailing date of the final rejection. The variable reply period procedure does not apply where SSP is less than 3 months (e.g., reissue litigation 1-month SSP, or reexamination proceedings). See MPEP § 710.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory-action processing when applicant files first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period and applicant files a complete first reply within 2 months of the final Office action, the examiner must determine if the reply: (1) places the application in condition for allowance; (2) places application in condition for allowance except for matters of form that examiner can change without authorization; or (3) does not place application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (1) or (2), process as allowance and no extension fees are due (for (2) see MPEP § 1302.04). If (3), the advisory action should inform applicant that SSP for reply expires 3 months from date of final rejection or mailing date of advisory action, by checking box 1.b) on PTOL-303. If the applicant files reply within 2 months but examiner mails advisory action after 3-month period, SSP expires at mailing of advisory action and extension fee calculation follows MPEP § 710.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory-action processing when applicant does not file complete first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period and applicant does NOT file a complete first reply within 2 months, examiners should check box 1.a) at top of PTOL-303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When box 1.b) is checked, time to take further action begins to run 3 months from date of final rejection or mailing date of advisory action, whichever is later; extension fees cannot be prorated; statutory period cannot exceed 6 months from the date of final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments after final — when allowed without extension fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complete first reply to a final Office action has been filed within 2 months, an examiner’s amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without payment of extension fees even if the amendment is made more than 3 months from the date of the final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the examiner’s amendment may not be made more than 6 months from the date of the final Office action, as the application would be abandoned by operation of law. If a complete first reply has not been filed within 2 months, applicant’s authorization to make an amendment to place the application in condition for allowance must be made either within the 3-month SSP or within an extended period with petition/fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a). An examiner’s amendment correcting only formal matters identified for the first time after a reply would not require any extension fee. See MPEP § 706.07(f)(F)-(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time and charging fees for examiner’s amendment (authorization rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17). Where an extension is necessary to place an application in condition for allowance, applicant may file the petition and fee or authorize the examiner to make the petition of record and charge a specified deposit account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office employees may not accept oral (telephonic) instructions to complete credit card payment or otherwise charge a patent process fee to a credit card. When authorization is given to make a petition of record, the authorization must be made of record in an examiner’s amendment indicating the person making authorization, when given, deposit account number, length of extension requested and amount to be charged. Use Form Paragraph 13.02.02 for telephone-authorized extensions. See MPEP § 706.07(f)(H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice after final — prompt processing and reply eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly by all Office personnel. Replies after final should not be considered by the examiner unless they are filed within the SSP or accompanied by a petition for an extension of time and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17 and 37 CFR 1.136(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement also applies to supplemental replies filed after the first reply. See MPEP § 706.07(f)(I)-(J).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final without extension fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be conducted after the expiration of the shortened statutory period for reply to a final Office action but within the 6-month statutory period for reply without the payment of an extension fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(f)(K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal matters identified after reply (Ex parte Quayle practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal matters identified for the first time after a reply is made to a final Office action and which require action by applicant to correct may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extension fees are required since the reply puts the application in condition for allowance except for correction of formal matters that had not yet been required by the examiner. See MPEP § 706.07(f)(L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after reply — withdraw finality to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is to be reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, the finality of the previous Office action should be withdrawn to avoid the issue of abandonment and the payment of extension fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a new reference renders a claim unpatentable after reply, the Office action should begin with a statement withdrawing finality and set forth the new ground of rejection (form paragraph 7.42 could be used). See MPEP § 706.07(f)(M) and § 706.07(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional after-final practice eligibility under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant in an application (other than reissue or design) pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995 (taking into account references to earlier-filed applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 and 365(c)) is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after a final rejection if the first submission and the fee in § 1.17(r) are filed prior to the filing of an appeal brief and prior to abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finality is automatically withdrawn upon timely filing of the submission and payment of the fee. Applicant may have up to two submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a) if conditions met. The transitional practice is only available to applications filed on or before June 8, 1995 and is not available for reissue, design applications, or reexamination proceedings. A 'submission' includes IDS, amendments to specification/claims/drawings, new substantive arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability. See MPEP § 706.07(g)(a) and related notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.41.01 — Transitional After Final Practice, First Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: This form paragraph notifies applicant that application qualifies under 37 CFR 1.129(a): since application pending at least two years as of June 8, 1995 (accounting for earlier-filed applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c)), applicant is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits if submission and fee in 37 CFR 1.17(r) are filed prior to filing appeal brief and prior to abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use in design or reissue applications, or in reexamination proceedings. Bracketed items require current fee and entity-size insertion. No amendment considered due to payment of fee may introduce new matter (35 U.S.C. 132). If multiple conflicting proposed amendments, provide specific instructions for entry. See examiner notes for usage and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponsive submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) — shortened time to reply (Form paragraph 7.42.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the timely submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) is not fully responsive to the prior Office action because [reason], applicant is given a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS from the mailing date of this letter, whichever is longer, to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The shortened period supersedes the prior time period and may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If a notice of appeal and appeal fee were filed prior to or with payment of the 1.17(r) fee, payment of 1.17(r) is construed as request to dismiss the appeal and continue prosecution. Examiner must state reasons why submission is not fully responsive in the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality after 1.129(a) submission (Form paragraph 7.42.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is eligible for 37 CFR 1.129(a) and the fee 1.17(r) has been timely paid, the finality of the previous Office action is withdrawn pursuant to 37 CFR 1.129(a). Applicant’s submission after final filed on [date] has been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert 'first' or 'second' as appropriate. If Notice of Appeal and appeal fee were filed prior to or with payment of 1.17(r), payment is construed as request to dismiss appeal and continue prosecution. Upon timely payment, if examiner determines submission not fully responsive (e.g., only an IDS), applicant is given a new shortened statutory period to reply. Previously unentered submissions are entered in order upon timely payment absent instructions; conditional payments treated as unconditional. Use form paragraph 7.42.01 to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action is final following 1.129(a) submission filed prior to June 8, 2005 (Form paragraph 7.42.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the application prior to the entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) and could have been finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered prior to entry under 37 CFR 1.129(a). Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action after the submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is reminded of extension policy 37 CFR 1.136(a). A shortened statutory period for reply is set to expire THREE MONTHS from mailing date; if first reply filed within TWO MONTHS and advisory action mailed after the 3-month SSP, the SSP expires on advisory mailing date; statutory period cannot exceed SIX MONTHS from mailing date. See MPEP § 706.07(g) and form paragraph usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second submission entitlement under 37 CFR 1.129(a) (Form paragraph 7.41.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the fee 37 CFR 1.17(r) for a first submission has been previously paid, applicant is entitled to have a second submission entered and considered on the merits if, prior to abandonment, the second submission and the fee are filed prior to filing an appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon timely filing of second submission and fee, finality of previous Office action is withdrawn. Payment construed as request to dismiss appeal if appeal filed previously. No amendment considered due to payment may introduce new matter (35 U.S.C. 132). Form paragraph should not be used in design or reissue applications or reexamination proceedings. If the fee has been twice paid, provisions of 1.129(a) no longer available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action final following 1.129(a) submission filed on/after June 8, 2005 (Form paragraph 7.42.031)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under final action practice for Office actions following a submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) filed on/after June 8, 2005, the next Office action following timely filing of a submission will be equivalent to the next Office action following a reply to a non-final Office action and will be made final, except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant’s amendment nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during 37 CFR 1.97(c) with fee 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no such new ground is introduced, the action is made final; applicant reminded of extension policy and SSP timing rules (3-month SSP, 2-month early-reply consideration, statutory limit 6 months). See MPEP § 706.07(g) and § 706.07(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Continued Examination (RCE) practice and eligibility (37 CFR 1.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution in an application is closed, an applicant may request continued examination by filing a submission and the fee set forth in § 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of: (1) payment of the issue fee (unless petition under § 1.313 granted); (2) abandonment; or (3) filing of a notice of appeal to the CAFC or commencement of civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146 (unless appeal/civil action is terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 'Prosecution is closed' means application is under appeal, last Office action is final (§ 1.113), notice of allowance (§ 1.311), or action that otherwise closes prosecution. A 'submission' includes IDS, amendments to written description/claims/drawings, new arguments, or new evidence; if reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, submission must meet reply requirements of § 1.111. Timely filed submission and fee will withdraw finality and the submission will be entered and considered. Filing an RCE after appeal but prior to decision treats it as request to withdraw appeal and reopen prosecution. An appeal brief or reply brief will not be considered a submission under this section. The provisions do not apply to provisional applications; certain pre-June 8, 1995 utility/plant or international applications; design patents; or patents under reexamination. See 37 CFR 1.114(a)-(e) and MPEP § 706.07(h).
